Rubio, a potential presidential candidate in 2028, declined to discuss his plans.

item.description: The six-day pause from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky comes as the administration ramps up efforts to secure an agreement to end the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Three in four displaced people live in climate danger zones, UN says
item.description: Nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people, or three-quarters of the global total, live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, the UN refugee agency said on Friday, urging action ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey. It said droughts, floods and extreme heat were making lasting solutions harder to find.

item.title: WATCH: Jaguars face injury-ravaged Ravens in Thursday Night Football matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler previews the Jaguars-Ravens matchup, Baltimore’s quarterback injuries and Trevor Lawrence’s strong start to the season.

item.title: Who won the redistricting war? So far, it looks like Democrats
item.description: Dems were able to keep seats that Republicans redrew to make them GOP-friendly.

item.title: Nigeria court bars opposition candidate two months before election
item.description: In tonight's edition, a Nigerian court disqualifies a leading presidential candidate, adding fresh complications for the electoral process two months before the election. Also, tens of thousands have fled across the border into Kenya as deadly ethnic clashes in southern Ethiopia intensify. And having fled conflict and violence, members of the first Refugee Youth Olympic Team are chasing Olympic dreams at Dakar 2026.

item.title: 'Extinction-level event': How Republicans eyeing 2028 are taking midterm losses
item.description: Republicans considering a presidential run offered their assessment of the party's performance in the midterm elections.

item.title: Judge blasts administration for planning to deport Iranians to Iran during wartime
item.description: The Trump administration said during a hearing that it's been making plans to deport Iranian migrants back to Iran during the war, earning a rebuke from a federal judge.

item.title: French protests: 'It's only when public, private sector act together that you can make changes'
item.description: “You can be as repressive as you want. The grievances are still here.” With this stark observation, Ariane Bogain, lecturer in French and politics at Northumbria University, captures the central dilemma confronting the French government: how can political authority be restored when the social and economic grievances driving public anger remain unresolved? Bogain and French politics editor Marc Perelman join Delano D'Souza to examine a protest movement that has evolved beyond its initial demands over purchasing power, fuel prices and education into a broader challenge to the French government. Perelman identifies a striking political paradox: Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, despite occupying opposing ideological positions, are “objective allies” in their shared electoral interest in weakening the political centre.

item.title: Appeals court weighs Trump's challenge to 2024 criminal hush money conviction
item.description: Two and a half years after a jury convicted Donald Trump of 34 felony counts in his hush money case, the president's lawyers are seeking to have the verdict overturned.

item.title: 'Inhumane punishment': Governor Gavin Newsom to commute all 548 California death sentences
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom on Thursday said he would commute all 548 death sentences in the state to life in prison without parole, marking a major step away from capital punishment as he prepares to leave office after eight years.

item.title: Breakaway league LIV Golf to fold after filing for bankruptcy
item.description: Breakaway men's league LIV Golf is to fold instead of launching a new version because of a lack of financial support.

item.title: 3rd place Mississippi Senate candidate says he did not spoil tight race for Democrat
item.description: The independent third place candidate in Mississippi's tight Senate race, Ty Pinkins, says he did not spoil the race.

item.title: Family of footballer who died after on-pitch collision pay tribute to him
item.description: Family, friends and teammates gathered for the funeral of the Spanish footballer who died following an on-field collision with another player.

item.description: Paraguayan lawmakers voted to impeach President Santiago Peña minutes after his resignation, as the collapse of a digital bank tied to his government froze millions of people's savings.

item.description: Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday he was retiring from international football at the age of 41.

item.description: The head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, Harmeet Dhillon, is out after 18 tumultuous months in charge.

item.description: President Donald Trump said he intends to keep Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in his job, as Rep. Massie, prepares to introduce an impeachment resolution against him.

item.title: France needs 'more public services', 'salaries are too low', 'schools are in very, very bad shape'
item.description: As France confronts another wave of strikes and protests, Gaëlle Martinez, National Secretary of the trade union Solidaires, presents the general strike as more than a confrontation over wages, public spending or the cost of living. Her account reveals a deeper struggle over economic dignity, the future of public services and the democratic right to collective protest. “People just want to live, not survive.” For Martinez, deteriorating schools, insufficient salaries and the dismantling of public services are not isolated policy failures. They are interconnected symptoms of political and economic priorities that, in her assessment, place fiscal restraint above social welfare. Her demand for “a new budget” that is “not based on cuts” is accompanied by a call to “tax the biggest companies, the richest companies where the profits are made.”

item.title: Paraguay's president Peña impeached moments after resigning over banking scandal
item.description: Paraguay’s lower house voted unanimously to impeach President Santiago Peña on Thursday, just minutes after he announced his resignation on X. Protesters have rallied in the streets since the takeover of a bank linked to Peña blocked millions of people, including pensioners, from accessing their money.

item.description: Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, explains what's behind the decrease in prices.

item.title: Discursive Verses: Is 'Spend Dat' the best financial indicator of America's grift economy?
item.description: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: How Yung Miami's summer bop became a sweeping indictment.

item.title: Russell Brand is convicted of rape, and judge says he'll get a prison term
item.description: A prosecutor described Brand as a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator." Brand, 51, denied the charges, saying he had never forced anyone to do something against their will.

item.title: Navi Pillay: Fighting violence with justice
item.description: From the International Criminal Court to Africa’s place in the global justice system, the stakes are high. In an exclusive interview, Nobel Peace Prize winner, Navi Pillay will discuss international justice . She says it it must not be held hostage to political power, as Donald Trump targets the ICC. What does this showdown mean for Africa?

item.title: US midterms: 'Donald Trump's wings have been more than clipped'
item.description: US President Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday's (November 3) midterms. The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump, leaving him as a lame duck president for the remaining two years of his term. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.title: Global travel sector grows despite headwinds
item.description: The global tourism sector is growing, despite conflicts and economic uncertainty. That's the finding of a new report by World Travel Market, which says the number of international arrivals is set to hit a record 1.57 billion in 2026.

item.title: Europe: Dozens of flights diverted following bomb threats
item.description: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 affected flights around Europe this week.

item.title: 'Identity crisis': Can Democrats 'deliver' following their 'historic', once in a generation victory?
item.description: A historic Democratic electoral breakthrough has transformed the American political landscape. For Laurie Dundon, Senior Associate Fellow at the European Leadership Network and former US diplomat, the central question is whether the Democratic Party can convert electoral momentum into coherent governance. "Can they deliver?" Dunden examines the apparent disintegration of Donald Trump's 2024 MAGA coalition alongside the Democratic Party's continuing ideological struggle between its progressive and centrist wings. Ahead of 2028, Dunden cautions against seeing Trump as a lame duck: "Trump is never going to stop being Trump." The resulting struggle over congressional spending powers, presidential vetoes, tariffs and investigations promises to be a delicate dance to watch".

item.description: Governor Gavin Newsom said he'll commute all death sentences in the state to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

item.title: WATCH: New 911 calls and bodycam video released in Citibank Center shooting in Tampa
item.description: A Citibank employee was shot and killed at a business complex in Florida on Wednesday, according to local authorities and company officials.

item.title: Israel's Arab list backs Eisenkot as Netanyahu loses ultra-Orthodox support
item.description: Israel's largest Arab party grouping said Thursday it would recommend opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, potentially bolstering his bid after Arab-majority lists won a record 19 seats in last week's election and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lost the support of an allied religious party.

item.title: WATCH: Eiffel Tower closes amid protests in Paris
item.description: ABC News’ Tom Soufi Burridge reports from Paris, where tens of thousands of police officers have been deployed to help maintain law and order.

item.title: Bringing the magic of Harry Potter to life through music
item.description: In this edition of Entre Nous, we meet Timothy Henty, the British conductor bringing the magic of Harry Potter to life in Paris. As part of the Harry Potter Film Concert Series, he leads more than 80 musicians in a spectacular live orchestral performance, offering audiences a unique opportunity to experience one of cinema's most beloved stories like never before.

item.title: British comedian Russell Brand found guilty of rape, sexual assault
item.description: A London jury on Thursday convicted British comedian and actor Russell Brand of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

item.title: France faces new protests as government seeks to prevent violence
item.description: France faces new protests as the government seeks to prevent a repeat of October unrest. Protesters demand better public services, including education, and also critique the rising cost-of-living. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin reports from the ground.

item.title: French bank hit by cyberattack, hackers steal $100 million
item.description: French regional bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said Wednesday it had been hit by a cyberattack that led to fraudulent transfers worth around 100 million euros ($112 million). The bank said the attack, which has since been "contained", allowed hackers to access its own accounts and transfer funds to other banks. Customer accounts were not affected, and no losses were reported by clients.

item.title: British doctor with Ebola returns to UK for treatment
item.description: A British doctor who tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has returned to the UK for treatment.

item.title: South African star Zolani Mahola: From 'Waka Waka' with Shakira to 'People Power'
item.description: From the global success of "Waka Waka" to her forthcoming second solo album "People Power", South Africa's Zolani Mahola has built a career around the power of music to bring people together.

item.title: 'It's fascinating to see a human becoming a person': Author Clémentine Goldszal
item.description: What is life like for a newly born, premature or sick baby? These are the questions tackled by a French journalist in her first ever book. Clémentine Goldszal asks what it means to be rushed from the delivery room to the neonatal intensive care unit, and what is means to enter the world before you are ready. Goldszal's book is entitled "Newborn: Inside the World of Neonatal Care". She spoke to us in Perspective.

item.title: Bent on leaving his mark: Trump's proposed 'Triumphal Arch' sparks backlash
item.description: Since his return to power, US President Donald Trump has been intent on reshaping the nation's capital Washington, seeking to leave his name and mark on it. After his involvement with the Kennedy Center, the White House ballroom and the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, Trump is now particularly keen on building a 250-foot (79-metre) "Triumphal Arch" – a project he claims is intended to honour the 250th anniversary of the United States.

item.title: What comes next for Democrats after midterm election victory?
item.description: With the US midterms over, Democrats are turning to what could become one of their most crowded and unpredictable presidential primaries in decades – a 2028 contest ​likely to expose the party's divide over how to win back the White House. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.description: After an Election Day so pivotal that votes were even being cast from space, there were many expressive reactions shared online.

item.description: The Senate race between Cindy Hyde-Smith and Scott Colom remains uncalled. Mississippi election law does not provide for automatic or requested recounts.
